claim: Takeuchi's Theorem 3 (1977) gives the complete, exhaustive list of all 85 arithmetic triangle-group triples (e1,e2,e3), and this verbatim list explicitly contains both (2,8,8) and (3,3,12).
stance_target: existence of the {(2,8,8),(3,3,12)} coincidence in the triangle-group/covolume literature
scope_conditions: compact-type arithmetic triangle groups, primary source read in full

claim: A triangle group (e1,e2,e3) is arithmetic iff it is commensurable with the unit group of an order in a quaternion algebra over a totally real number field; the criterion (Theorem 1) is expressed via the trace field k0=Q((cos(pi/e1))^2,(cos(pi/e2))^2,(cos(pi/e3))^2, cos(pi/e1)cos(pi/e2)cos(pi/e3)) and an embedding-positivity inequality, entirely independent of the numeric sum e1+e2+e3 or the reciprocal sum 1/e1+1/e2+1/e3.
stance_target: mechanism determining Takeuchi's list, to clarify it is not driven by the reciprocal-sum coincidence

claim: Takeuchi's 1977 paper (the primary source establishing the 85-triple list) explicitly states in its closing remark that it does NOT classify those 85 triples by commensurability class, deferring that task; the commensurability classification appears only in a companion 1977 paper that could not be located online in this fetch pass.
stance_target: whether (2,8,8) and (3,3,12) are mutually commensurable (same quaternion algebra)
quoted_support: It remains to classify all triples listed in Theorem 3 with respect to the commensurability. In the non-compact case this is trivial because these groups are all commensurable with some conjugate group of the modular group.
numbers: 19 commensurability classes (per secondary web-search synthesis, unverified against primary source)
entities: J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo Sect. IA Math. 24 (1977) 201-212

claim: By the Gauss-Bonnet theorem, the hyperbolic area (covolume) of a triangle group (e1,e2,e3) is proportional to 1-(1/e1+1/e2+1/e3); since 1/2+1/8+1/8 = 1/3+1/3+1/12 = 3/4 exactly, the triangle orbifolds (2,8,8) and (3,3,12) have identical covolume as a direct algebraic consequence of the paper's equal-reciprocal-sum condition, making 'equal reciprocal sum' and 'equal covolume' the same fact for this pair, not merely analogous framings.
stance_target: the dual number-theoretic / triangle-group-covolume framing of Section 5's coincidence
quoted_support: the hyperbolic area of the (e1,e2,e3) triangle is proportional to 1 - (1/e1+1/e2+1/e3) (i.e. proportional to minus the orbifold Euler characteristic)

claim: Takeuchi's list (Theorem 3) reproduces, for the sub-families of type (2,3,e3), (2,4,e3) and (2,6,e3), the earlier list already given by Fricke and Klein (Vorlesungen uber die Theorie der automorphen Funktionen I, 1897) pp.610-611, showing the arithmeticity of some triangle groups was known observationally as early as 1897, decades before Takeuchi's systematic classification.
stance_target: historical depth of the arithmetic-triangle-group literature
quoted_support: As to the triples of types (2,3,e3), (2,4,e3) and (2,6,e3), our result coincides with the list of [Fricke-Klein] pp.610-611.
